claim: Microglia and infiltrating macrophages are amongst the most abundant cell types in the microenvironment of brain tumours.
source: Microglia and infiltrating macrophages are amongst the most abundant cell types in the microenvironment of brain tumours and have been shown to actively promote tumour growth (Hambardzumyan et al., 2016; Quail and Joyce, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Hambardzumyan et al., 2016 and Quail and Joyce, 2017

claim: Microglia and infiltrating macrophages have been shown to actively promote tumour growth.
source: Microglia and infiltrating macrophages are amongst the most abundant cell types in the microenvironment of brain tumours and have been shown to actively promote tumour growth (Hambardzumyan et al., 2016; Quail and Joyce, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Hambardzumyan et al., 2016 and Quail and Joyce, 2017

claim: Modifications of the extracellular matrix contribute to tumour-promoting activity of microglia and macrophages.
source: A variety of mechanism contribute to this tumour-promoting activity including modifications of the extracellular matrix, the induction of angiogenesis and the generation of an immunosuppressive environment (Markovic et al., 2005; Komohara et al., 2008; Wu et al., 2010; Zhai et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2012; Ellert-Miklaszewska et al., 2013; Pyonteck et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2013; Hambardzumyan et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: The induction of angiogenesis contributes to tumour-promoting activity of microglia and macrophages.
source: A variety of mechanism contribute to this tumour-promoting activity including modifications of the extracellular matrix, the induction of angiogenesis and the generation of an immunosuppressive environment (Markovic et al., 2005; Komohara et al., 2008; Wu et al., 2010; Zhai et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2012; Ellert-Miklaszewska et al., 2013; Pyonteck et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2013; Hambardzumyan et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: The generation of an immunosuppressive environment contributes to tumour-promoting activity of microglia and macrophages.
source: A variety of mechanism contribute to this tumour-promoting activity including modifications of the extracellular matrix, the induction of angiogenesis and the generation of an immunosuppressive environment (Markovic et al., 2005; Komohara et al., 2008; Wu et al., 2010; Zhai et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2012; Ellert-Miklaszewska et al., 2013; Pyonteck et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2013; Hambardzumyan et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: Direct cellular interactions between microglia and brain tumour cells have been described.
source: Intriguingly, direct cellular interactions between microglia and brain tumour cells have been described (Bayerl et al., 2016; Hamilton et al., 2016; Resende et al., 2016; Ricard et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claim: Cellular interactions between microglia and tumour cells consist of different types of direct surface contacts.
source: These cellular interactions consist of different types of direct surface contacts between microglia and tumour cells, from microglia constantly extending processes towards tumour cells to microglia flattening their surfaces around tumour cells.
evidence: Described in the manuscript text

claim: Microglia-tumour cell interactions were long-lasting and did not appear to be anti-tumoural as phagocytic events were not observed.
source: Importantly, these interactions were long-lasting and did not appear to be anti-tumoural as phagocytic events were not observed.
evidence: Based on observations described in cited studies

claim: Microglia-tumour cell interactions have been consistently observed in a variety of models of orthotopic transplantations of human and mouse glioma cells into mouse or zebrafish brains.
source: These observations have been consistently made in a variety of models of orthotopic transplantations of human and mouse glioma cells into mouse or zebrafish brains (Bayerl et al., 2016; Hamilton et al., 2016; Resende et al., 2016; Ricard et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claim: Cellular interactions between microglia and pre-neoplastic AKT1+ cells can be observed during the earliest stages of tumour growth.
source: Furthermore, we have recently shown that these cellular interactions are initiated during the earliest stages of tumour growth as they can already be observed between microglia and pre-neoplastic AKT1+ cells (Chia et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chia et al., 2018

claim: Microglia direct cellular processes towards neurons with increased intracellular Ca2+ levels.
source: Microglia have been observed to direct cellular processes towards neurons with increased intracellular Ca2+ levels (Li et al., 2012; Sieger et al., 2012; Eyo et al., 2014; Eyo et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claim: Microglia-neuron interactions are regulated by ATP/ADP released from neurons upon intracellular Ca2+ increase.
source: These interactions were regulated by ATP/ADP released from the neurons upon intracellular Ca2+ increase and sensed by the microglia via the purinergic P2y12 receptor (Li et al., 2012; Sieger et al., 2012; Eyo et al., 2014; Eyo et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claim: Microglia sense ATP/ADP via the purinergic P2y12 receptor.
source: These interactions were regulated by ATP/ADP released from the neurons upon intracellular Ca2+ increase and sensed by the microglia via the purinergic P2y12 receptor (Li et al., 2012; Sieger et al., 2012; Eyo et al., 2014; Eyo et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claim: Microglia were observed to cluster in areas of AKT1+ cells.
source: As described previously, microglia were observed to cluster in areas of AKT1+ cells while their distribution appeared normal in fish injected with the lexOP:tagRFP control construct (Figure 1A,B, Figure 1—videos 1 and 2).
evidence: Supported by observations in Figure 1A,B and videos

claim: Microglia distribution appeared normal in fish injected with the lexOP:tagRFP control construct.
source: As described previously, microglia were observed to cluster in areas of AKT1+ cells while their distribution appeared normal in fish injected with the lexOP:tagRFP control construct (Figure 1A,B, Figure 1—videos 1 and 2).
evidence: Supported by observations in Figure 1A,B and videos

claim: Microglia showed a significantly increased number of direct interactions with AKT1+ cells compared to control cells.
source: Importantly, microglia showed a significantly increased number of direct interactions with AKT1+ cells compared to control cells (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by quantification shown in Figure 1C

claim: Two or more microglial cells were frequently observed to interact with the same AKT1+ cell.
source: Furthermore, two or more microglial cells were frequently observed to interact with the same AKT1+ cell (Figure 1E, Figure 1—video 4).
evidence: Supported by observations in Figure 1E and video 4

claim: Overexpression of HRASV12 in neural cells stimulated similar microglial responses as AKT1 overexpression.
source: Interestingly, overexpression of HRASV12 in neural cells as well as overexpression of AKT1 and HRASV12 under control of the zic4 enhancer stimulated similar microglial responses (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by observations in Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: Overexpression of AKT1 and HRASV12 under control of the zic4 enhancer stimulated similar microglial responses.
source: Interestingly, overexpression of HRASV12 in neural cells as well as overexpression of AKT1 and HRASV12 under control of the zic4 enhancer stimulated similar microglial responses (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by observations in Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: AKT1+ cells have significantly increased Ca2+ levels compared to control cells.
source: Indeed, these quantifications showed a steady increase of Ca2+ levels in AKT1+ cells compared to control cells over time (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: Supported by quantifications shown in Figure 2A-C

claim: Ca2+ levels were significantly increased in AKT1+ cells from four dpf onwards.
source: Ca2+ levels were significantly increased in AKT1+ cells from four dpf onwards and showed a drastic increase at 7 dpf (Figure 2C).
evidence: Supported by quantifications shown in Figure 2C

claim: Ca2+ levels in AKT1+ cells showed a drastic increase at 7 dpf.
source: Ca2+ levels were significantly increased in AKT1+ cells from four dpf onwards and showed a drastic increase at 7 dpf (Figure 2C).
evidence: Supported by quantifications shown in Figure 2C

claim: In control RFP cells, calcium activity was observed to be relatively static over time.
source: In control RFP cells, calcium activity was observed to be relatively static over time (n = 35 larvae analysed; Figure 2D, Figure 2—video 1).
evidence: Supported by observations in Figure 2D and video 1

claim: Approximately 31% of AKT1-positive cells were observed to strongly up- and down-regulate Ca2+ levels repeatedly.
source: Through the course of acquisition,~31% of AKT1-positive cells were observed to strongly up- and down-regulate Ca2+ levels (∆F/F0 increase >0.05) repeatedly, thus creating a firing pattern (n = 35 larvae analysed; Figure 2E, Figure 2—video 2).
evidence: Supported by observations in Figure 2E and video 2

claim: Dynamic changes in calcium firing were not detected in any of the analysed control RFP cells.
source: We did not detect these patterns in any of the analysed control RFP cells (n = 35 larvae analysed).
evidence: Based on analysis of 35 larvae

claim: Dynamic changes in calcium firing were more frequently observed in AKT1+ cells within close vicinity to other AKT1 expressing cells.
source: While these dynamic changes in calcium firing were specific to individual AKT1 positive cells, they were more frequently observed in cells within close vicinity to other AKT1 expressing cells.
evidence: Based on observations during analysis

claim: Microglia were detected directly responding to AKT1+ cells with increased Ca2+ levels.
source: Importantly, we detected microglia directly responding to AKT1+ cells with increased Ca2+ levels.
evidence: Based on observations in double transgenic larvae

claim: Prolonged cellular contacts were observed between microglia and AKT1+ cells with increased Ca2+ levels.
source: We observed prolonged cellular contacts between microglia and AKT1+ cells with increased Ca2+ levels (Figure 3A–D, arrows) as well as microglia sending processes towards AKT1+ cells that increased their Ca2+ levels during the time of the acquisition (Figure 3A–H, arrowheads).
evidence: Supported by observations in Figure 3A-D

claim: Microglia send processes towards AKT1+ cells that increased their Ca2+ levels during the time of acquisition.
source: We observed prolonged cellular contacts between microglia and AKT1+ cells with increased Ca2+ levels (Figure 3A–D, arrows) as well as microglia sending processes towards AKT1+ cells that increased their Ca2+ levels during the time of the acquisition (Figure 3A–H, arrowheads).
evidence: Supported by observations in Figure 3A-H

claim: Inhibition of NMDA receptor signalling led to a significant reduction of Ca2+ levels in AKT1+ cells.
source: Inhibition of NMDA receptor signalling led to a significant reduction of Ca2+ levels in AKT1+ cells compared to the AKT1+ cells in untreated larvae (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by quantifications shown in Figure 4A

claim: Inhibition of NMDA receptor signalling led to a significant reduction in the number of microglial interactions with AKT1+ cells.
source: In line with the reduction of Ca2+ levels we detected a significant reduction in the number of microglial interactions with AKT1+ cells (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by quantifications shown in Figure 4B

claim: Increased Ca2+ levels in AKT1+ cells are required to attract microglial processes.
source: Thus, increased Ca2+ levels in AKT1+ cells are required to attract microglial processes.
evidence: Inferred from the reduction of microglial interactions upon NMDA receptor inhibition

claim: Inhibiting pannexin channels led to a significant reduction of cellular interactions between microglial cells and AKT1+ cells.
source: Indeed, inhibiting pannexin channels led to a significant reduction of cellular interactions between microglial cells and AKT1+ cells (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by quantifications shown in Figure 4C

claim: p2ry12 expression is highly specific to microglia in the brain.
source: Importantly, p2ry12 expression is highly specific to microglia in the brain and p2ry12 is considered to be a microglia signature gene (Crotti and Ransohoff, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Crotti and Ransohoff, 2016

claim: p2ry12 is considered to be a microglia signature gene.
source: Importantly, p2ry12 expression is highly specific to microglia in the brain and p2ry12 is considered to be a microglia signature gene (Crotti and Ransohoff, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Crotti and Ransohoff, 2016

claim: Acute injection of the p2ry12 gRNA efficiently mutated the p2ry12 gene.
source: Acute injection of the p2ry12 gRNA efficiently mutated the p2ry12 gene as shown by restriction fragment length polymorphism (RFLP) analysis, while injection of a control gRNA did not cause mutation of the p2ry12 gene (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: Supported by RFLP analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B

claim: Injection of a control gRNA did not cause mutation of the p2ry12 gene.
source: Acute injection of the p2ry12 gRNA efficiently mutated the p2ry12 gene as shown by restriction fragment length polymorphism (RFLP) analysis, while injection of a control gRNA did not cause mutation of the p2ry12 gene (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: Supported by RFLP analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B

claim: The p2ry12 gRNA had a mutation rate approaching 100%.
source: RFLP analysis demonstrated the p2ry12 gRNA had a mutation rate approaching 100% (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: Supported by RFLP analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B

claim: Injection of p2ry12 gRNA abolished P2ry12-GFP expression on microglia.
source: Injection of p2ry12 gRNA into these fish did not, as expected, impact on mCherry expression on microglia (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C). However, P2ry12-GFP expression was clearly abolished on the microglia, revealing complete knockout of the P2ry12 protein (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by observations in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C

claim: In the p2ry12 crispant background microglia interactions with AKT1+ cells were significantly reduced.
source: Importantly, in the p2ry12 crispant background microglia interactions with AKT1+ cells were significantly reduced (Figure 4D).
evidence: Supported by quantifications shown in Figure 4D

claim: On average ~40% of microglia interacted with AKT1+ cells in p2ry12 wt brains.
source: Quantifications revealed that while on average ~40% of microglia interacted with AKT1+ cells in p2ry12 wt brains, only ~21% of microglia showed interactions with AKT1+ cells in the p2ry12 crispant background (Figure 4D).
evidence: Supported by quantifications shown in Figure 4D

claim: Only ~21% of microglia showed interactions with AKT1+ cells in the p2ry12 crispant background.
source: Quantifications revealed that while on average ~40% of microglia interacted with AKT1+ cells in p2ry12 wt brains, only ~21% of microglia showed interactions with AKT1+ cells in the p2ry12 crispant background (Figure 4D).
evidence: Supported by quantifications shown in Figure 4D

claim: P2ry12 signalling in microglia is required to mediate cellular interactions with AKT1+ cells.
source: In conclusion, these experiments show that P2ry12 signalling in microglia is required to mediate cellular interactions with AKT1+ cells.
evidence: Inferred from the reduction of interactions in p2ry12 crispant background

claim: AKT1+ cells showed significantly increased proliferation rates compared to control cells in wt brains.
source: As described previously, AKT1+ cells showed significantly increased proliferation rates compared to control cells in wt brains (Figure 5B) (Chia et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by quantifications shown in Figure 5B and citation to Chia et al., 2018

claim: No differences were detected in the proliferation rates of control RFP cells in p2ry12 crispant brains compared to p2yr12 wildtype brains.
source: In p2ry12 crispant brains no differences were detected in the proliferation rates of control RFP cells compared to p2yr12 wildtype brains (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by quantifications shown in Figure 5B

claim: There was an almost 50% drop in the proliferation rate of AKT1+ cells in p2ry12 crispant brains compared to p2ry12 wildtype brains.
source: However, we found an almost 50% drop in the proliferation rate of AKT1+ cells in p2ry12 crispant brains compared to p2ry12 wildtype brains (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by quantifications shown in Figure 5B

claim: Numbers of microglia were similar in p2ry12 crispant brains and p2yr12 wildtype brains.
source: As numbers of microglia were similar in p2ry12 crispant brains and p2yr12 wildtype brains (Figure 5A), we conclude that the reduced number of interactions in p2ry12 crispant brains was the reason for the decrease in proliferation of AKT1 cells.
evidence: Supported by quantifications shown in Figure 5A

claim: The reduced number of interactions in p2ry12 crispant brains was the reason for the decrease in proliferation of AKT1 cells.
source: As numbers of microglia were similar in p2ry12 crispant brains and p2yr12 wildtype brains (Figure 5A), we conclude that the reduced number of interactions in p2ry12 crispant brains was the reason for the decrease in proliferation of AKT1 cells.
evidence: Inferred from the similar microglia numbers but reduced proliferation

claim: Microglia interactions directly promote proliferation of pre-neoplastic AKT1 cells.
source: Thus, microglia interactions directly promote proliferation of pre-neoplastic AKT1 cells.
evidence: Inferred from the reduced proliferation when interactions are reduced

claim: Pre-neoplastic cells hijack the same mechanism used by neurons to attract microglial processes.
source: Here, we showed that pre-neoplastic cells hijack the same mechanism to attract microglial processes.
evidence: Based on the experimental results showing Ca2+-ATP-P2ry12 signalling

claim: Increased Ca2+ levels in AKT1+ cells, the release of ATP from these cells and P2ry12 signalling on microglia are required to stimulate microglial interactions with AKT1+ cells.
source: We showed that increased Ca2+ levels in AKT1+ cells, the release of ATP from these cells and P2ry12 signalling on microglia are required to stimulate microglial interactions with AKT1+ cells.
evidence: Based on the experimental results from pharmacological and genetic manipulations

claim: Direct cellular interactions between microglia and pre-neoplastic cells are a cause of increased proliferation.
source: Here, we identify direct cellular interactions between microglia and pre-neoplastic cells as a cause of increased proliferation.
evidence: Based on the experimental results showing reduced proliferation when interactions are reduced

claim: Cellular interactions between macrophages and melanoma cells result in the transfer of cytoplasm from macrophages to melanoma cells.
source: Roh-Johnson et al. showed direct cellular contacts between macrophages and melanoma cells (Roh-Johnson et al., 2017). These cellular contacts resulted in the transfer of cytoplasm from macrophages to melanoma cells which led to an increased dissemination of the melanoma cells (Roh-Johnson et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Roh-Johnson et al., 2017

claim: Transfer of cytoplasm from macrophages to melanoma cells led to an increased dissemination of the melanoma cells.
source: These cellular contacts resulted in the transfer of cytoplasm from macrophages to melanoma cells which led to an increased dissemination of the melanoma cells (Roh-Johnson et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Roh-Johnson et al., 2017

claim: Macrophage contacts with breast cancer cells induce RhoA GTPase signalling within the cancer cells.
source: Furthermore, macrophage contacts with breast cancer cells have been shown to induce RhoA GTPase signalling within the cancer cells and to trigger their intravasation (Roh-Johnson et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Roh-Johnson et al., 2014

claim: Macrophage contacts with breast cancer cells trigger their intravasation.
source: Furthermore, macrophage contacts with breast cancer cells have been shown to induce RhoA GTPase signalling within the cancer cells and to trigger their intravasation (Roh-Johnson et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Roh-Johnson et al., 2014

claim: Microglial processes may alter the Ca2+ levels within the pre-neoplastic cells which might trigger changes in their proliferative capacities.
source: We hypothesise that microglial processes alter the Ca2+ levels within the pre-neoplastic cells which might trigger changes in their proliferative capacities.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors

claim: Ca2+-dependent increase in transcription factors are crucial for cellular division, proliferation, as well as cancer cell survival.
source: This is in line with previous studies showing a Ca2+-dependent increase in transcription factors which are crucial for cellular division, proliferation, as well as cancer cell survival (reviewed by Roderick and Cook, 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Roderick and Cook, 2008

claim: AKT1+ cells within close vicinity to other AKT1 expressing cells showed an increased frequency of fluctuations in their Ca2+ levels.
source: Interestingly, cells that were within close vicinity to other AKT1 expressing cells showed an increased frequency of fluctuations in their Ca2+ levels.
evidence: Based on observations during analysis

claim: Astrocytoma cells form a functional network which is connected via tumour microtubes (TMs).
source: Interestingly, in an elegant in vivo study, astrocytoma cells have been shown to form a functional network which is connected via tumour microtubes (TMs) (Osswald et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Osswald et al., 2015

claim: Astrocytoma cells within the network showed survival benefits and resistance against radiotherapy.
source: Astrocytoma cells within the network showed survival benefits and resistance against radiotherapy (Osswald et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Osswald et al., 2015

claim: Dynamic Ca2+ transients have been observed within the astrocytoma network.
source: Importantly, dynamic Ca2+ transients have been observed within this network and a role for the network in brain invasion and proliferation has been described.
evidence: Based on the cited study on astrocytoma networks

claim: The astrocytoma network has a role in brain invasion and proliferation.
source: Importantly, dynamic Ca2+ transients have been observed within this network and a role for the network in brain invasion and proliferation has been described.
evidence: Based on the cited study on astrocytoma networks

claim: Microglia may contribute to the establishment of a functional network between tumour cells by promoting the outgrowth of TMs.
source: As we observed microglia to directly interact with these AKT1+ cells and their processes, we speculate that microglia contribute to the establishment of a functional network between tumour cells by promoting the outgrowth of TMs.
evidence: This is speculation by the authors

claim: Microglia promote neuronal survival and axonal growth by providing insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1).
source: Microglia have been shown for example to promote neuronal survival and axonal growth by providing insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) (Ueno et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ueno et al., 2013

claim: Expression of the P2y12 receptor is specific for microglia in the brain.
source: As expression of the P2y12 receptor, which mediates these interactions, is specific for microglia in the brain, pharmacological inhibition of the receptor might offer new routes for therapy to reduce proliferation of the tumour cells.
evidence: Based on established knowledge about P2y12 receptor expression

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of the P2y12 receptor might offer new routes for therapy to reduce proliferation of tumour cells.
source: As expression of the P2y12 receptor, which mediates these interactions, is specific for microglia in the brain, pharmacological inhibition of the receptor might offer new routes for therapy to reduce proliferation of the tumour cells.
evidence: This is speculation about potential therapeutic applications

claim: Neoplastic cells repurpose endogenous neuron to microglia signalling mechanisms to promote their own proliferation.
source: In conclusion, neoplastic cells repurpose the endogenous neuron to microglia signalling mechanism via P2ry12 activation to promote their own proliferation.
evidence: This is the main conclusion based on all experimental results

claim: Ca2+ transients in AKT1+ cells stimulate ATP-mediated interactions with microglia.
source: Using a combination of live imaging, genetic and pharmacological tools, we show that these Ca2+ transients stimulate ATP-mediated interactions with microglia.
evidence: Based on experimental results using multiple approaches

claim: Interfering with Ca2+ levels abolishes microglia-AKT1+ cell interactions.
source: Interfering with Ca2+ levels, inhibiting ATP release and CRISPR-mediated mutation of the p2ry12 locus abolishes these interactions.
evidence: Based on experimental results with NMDA receptor inhibition

claim: Inhibiting ATP release abolishes microglia-AKT1+ cell interactions.
source: Interfering with Ca2+ levels, inhibiting ATP release and CRISPR-mediated mutation of the p2ry12 locus abolishes these interactions.
evidence: Based on experimental results with CBX treatment

claim: CRISPR-mediated mutation of the p2ry12 locus abolishes microglia-AKT1+ cell interactions.
source: Interfering with Ca2+ levels, inhibiting ATP release and CRISPR-mediated mutation of the p2ry12 locus abolishes these interactions.
evidence: Based on experimental results with p2ry12 crispants

claim: Reducing the number of microglial interactions significantly impairs the proliferation of neoplastic AKT1 cells.
source: Finally, we show that reducing the number of microglial interactions significantly impairs the proliferation of neoplastic AKT1 cells.
evidence: Based on experimental results in p2ry12 crispants

claim: Cellular abnormalities and increased proliferation are detected in AKT1+ cells within the first week of development.
source: In this model, cellular abnormalities and increased proliferation are detected in AKT1+ cells within the first week of development and solid tumours can be observed from 1 month of age (Chia et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chia et al., 2018

claim: Solid tumours can be observed from 1 month of age in the AKT1 zebrafish model.
source: In this model, cellular abnormalities and increased proliferation are detected in AKT1+ cells within the first week of development and solid tumours can be observed from 1 month of age (Chia et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chia et al., 2018

claim: CBX treated larvae appeared inactive compared to controls and showed a reduced escape reaction upon mechanical stimulation.
source: CBX treated larvae appeared inactive compared to controls and showed a reduced escape reaction upon mechanical stimulation.
evidence: Based on observations during the experiment
